beginner.summary: For developers, operations engineers and SREs who are new to New Relic and need to instrument and watch real services on it. Covers accounts, entities and API key types, the infrastructure agent and on-host integrations, APM agents for Java, Python and Node.js, the APM summary and Apdex, first NRQL queries and dashboards, logs in context, browser monitoring and Core Web Vitals, ping and simple browser synthetics, distributed tracing, Errors Inbox, static NRQL alert conditions with workflows and destinations, user types and the basics of data ingest, and a capstone that monitors a three-tier demo application end to end.
prerequisites: Runs and deploys a simple web application written in Java, Python or Node.js and can read its logs
Uses a Linux shell with sudo, systemctl and curl, and can edit YAML and INI configuration files
Has a New Relic account (the free tier is enough) with an admin user, plus a Linux VM or laptop with Docker where agents can be installed
outcomes: Install and configure the New Relic infrastructure agent, on-host integrations and APM agents, and confirm data with NRQL
Read the APM summary, distributed traces, Errors Inbox and logs in context to find the cause of a slow or failing request
Write NRQL queries with FACET, TIMESERIES and COMPARE WITH and build a dashboard from them
Create static NRQL alert conditions and route issues through workflows to email, Slack or webhook destinations
